top3.whyItMatters: AI chat histories hold company secrets, so treat them as sensitive data and limit shared links.

top3.headline: DeepMind's planning assistant cut officer time 58% and now expands
top3.whyItMatters: A measured public-sector win on routine casework shows where agents pay off first.

top3.headline: Harrison Chase: agent design has converged, context problems have not
top3.whyItMatters: The edge is moving from agent architecture to how teams manage what agents see.

items.title: poteto: a few well-onboarded bots beat a large team
items.takeaway: Give bots tools, onboard them like an intern, and have them write their own skills.
items.soWhat: Treat agents like new hires: brief them well and have them write down how they work.

items.title: Harrison Chase maps new context engineering challenges for agents
items.takeaway: He argues teams have converged on one agent architecture while new context problems emerge.
items.soWhat: Competitive advantage is shifting from agent design to managing what agents see and remember.

items.title: DeepMind extends its planning assistant to 12 more English councils
items.takeaway: Pilots in three councils cut officer time on householder assessments by 58%; officers keep the decision.
items.soWhat: Routine, rule-heavy casework is where agents show measurable gains first, with humans signing off.

items.title: Ruben Hassid shares a Claude Code prompt to rebuild a reference site
items.takeaway: A /goal prompt points Claude Code at his public remake repo; the repo was not independently tested.
items.soWhat: Copying a site's look is becoming a single prompt, so differentiate on substance, not surface.

items.title: Opening a shared ChatGPT link could leak a user's private chats
items.takeaway: Parameter Labs found the flaw; OpenAI fixed it on Oct 26 and rated it P1.
items.soWhat: AI chat histories hold company secrets, so treat them as sensitive data and limit shared links.

voices.quote: It feels like everyone is converging on the same agent architecture: an LLM, running in a loop, calling tools, running in a sandbox.
you don’t need a lot of bots. a few good bots can be more useful and easier to manage than a large team

hotOnX.text: you don’t need a lot of bots. a few good bots can be more useful and easier to manage than a large team
